<!-- pr-reviewer: f99f045ecab7747c5eb55ec414fba3444ec92ebd -->
**Needs changes before merge.** One blocker: after a tool change the post assumes A is still where it left it. Everything else checks out.

### What looks good
- **Index order.** At a section's first motion the post writes `G53 G0 Z<safe>`, then `G0 A..` alone, then `G0 X Y` in the turned frame, and only then Z. The A word is written only in `indexFor` (assets/posts/tormach.cps:477-488), on a G0 line of its own. No cutting move can carry an A. Any A change inside a section is refused (the `aSection` check).
- **Frame math.** `tip()` applies Rx(-a) to (y, z), which takes the pose-law tool axis (0, -sin a, cos a) onto +Z. The test's `world()` is an independent hand rotation. With `[-1,0,0]` the posted word is negated (`ax.sign`). A0 B180 resolves to tool axis (0, 0, -1), which is the same physical pose as A180, so `G0 A180` is correct. The operator note about the WCS on the A centerline comes before the first index.
- **README direction check.** The MDI step (G0 A90: the front face comes to the top) matches the post's convention, because the part turns by Rx(-a).
- **Refusal pins are real.** I mutated two of them locally. With the indexed-arc refusal disabled, only `an_arc_on_an_indexed_a_is_refused` fails. With the travel refusal disabled, only `an_a_past_travel_is_refused` fails (9 pass / 1 fail each time).
- **Parser fix (`crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs:156`).** I compared the old and new head search on every tracked `.mch`. Only the new `tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` resolves differently: the old search lost its head, the new one finds it. No other shipped machine's parsed result changes. The direction is safe: a file that had silently lost its spindle limits and coolant now states them. It is pinned by `the_microarc_machine_states_an_a_about_x` (spindle, ranges, rigid tapping and coolants equal the 770MX).
- **Machines without A are unchanged.** `conformance` is green and no existing golden is touched. The only new goldens are `index_4face_microarc4.nc` and the kit `.nc`, which `microarc_test_part` pins byte-for-byte.
- **Laws.** The only Rust change (parse.rs) has no unwrap, expect or panic. Provenance is present (TD10749 / TD10552 / TD10374, LinuxCNC). New files are under 400 lines (the `.cps` is exempt). No `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNG, build.rs, `.github`, script or dependency changes. No process file is touched, since `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` is not one.

### Local results (merged with main d68d6d18, clean merge)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --no-run` | ok |
| tormach_fourth_axis | 10 passed |
| microarc_test_part | 2 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| machine | 33 passed |
| machine_library | 11 passed |
| machine_edit | 12 passed |
| tormach_post | 10 passed |
| tormach_machines | 6 passed |
| tormach_safe_retract | 4 passed |
| probe_tormach | 7 passed |
| tilt | 8 passed |

| posting | 17 passed |
| camcraft-post lib | 7 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **A is not restated after the G30 tool change. This can index the wrong face silently.**
   - The code: `retract()` writes a bare `G30` (assets/posts/tormach.cps:239) before every `T.. M6` (startPreamble, :342), but `aNow` survives it. `indexFor` then skips the index whenever the next section's A equals the held word (:477).
   - Why it matters: under LinuxCNC a G30 with no axis words rapids **all** axes to the stored G30 position, parameters 5181-5189, A included. PathPilot's stored A is whatever the operator set.
   - The app re-issues the tool before every operation, even the same tool (see the kit's `FLAT A90`, which gets `G30 / T1 M6` again). So any two consecutive ops on the same face trigger this, e.g. a rough and a finish at A90. The second op then cuts in the A90 frame with the table wherever G30 left it. That is a gouge with no diagnostic. The post's own comment says "a program never assumes where the last run left the table", and this breaks that rule.
   - Repro (a local probe, not committed): two sections, both at A90, T3 then T4. The second section posts `G53 G0 Z0 / G30 / T4 M6 / G43 H4 / M8 / G0 X0 Y0 / G0 X0 Y0 Z1.1811 / G1 ...` with no `G0 A90`.
   - Fix: set `aNow = null;` whenever the post writes G30 (in `retract()` next to the `G30`, or at the tool change in `startPreamble`). The next section then re-indexes with `G53 G0 Z / G0 A..`.
   - Pin it: add a test in `tormach_fourth_axis.rs` where two ops at the same non-zero A, with a tool change between, both get `G0 A..` after their `M6`. The kit `.nc` and the 4-face golden do not change, because every op there indexes anyway. Please re-check the README checklist item 7 ("A is left at 0") against the final `G30` as well.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **Swept clearance is not checked anywhere.** The index retracts to the highest Z the machine has (`G53 G0 Z0`), which is the best the post can do. But nothing checks that the tool tip at top of travel clears the radius swept by the part, chuck and jaws. On a 3/4" bar that is fine. A larger part or a long tool could hit while A turns. Consider adding a README safety step ("at `G53 Z0`, the tool tip clears the chuck's swept radius") and a follow-up issue for a swept-radius check in the program gate or the sim.
- **Spindle and coolant stay on while A turns.** `S.. M3 / M8` come before the index. That is probably fine, but the operator may prefer M5/M9 around the first index. This is a judgement call.
- **Travel check on canonical angles.** `toolAngle` returns (-180, 180], so on a machine stated 0..360 an A-90 face is refused even though A270 reaches it. The refusal is safe; I note it only for when another table is added.
- **Misplaced doc comment (already in main).** The comment `/// First part anywhere in the tree with the given type, depth-first.` sits over `parse_ranges` (parse.rs:129), not `find_type`. A one-line move would fix it while you are in the file.
- **No direct unit test for the parser fix.** It is pinned only through the shipped file's layout. A small unit test in `parse.rs` (a leaf ahead of the head) would keep it pinned if the file is reordered.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 14314261453daef76b4a4b72884f51c9c62c66ae -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a delta review of 14314261 ("fix(post): restate A after every G30 on the microARC 4"), on top of the earlier review of f99f045e. The blocker from that review is fixed and pinned.

### What looks good
- **The blocker is fixed.** `retract()` forgets A (`aNow = null`) right after the bare `G30` (assets/posts/tormach.cps:239-246). `endPreamble()` also forgets it at every section end (:372). So every section now opens with `G53 G0 Z<safe>` / `G0 A..`, with or without a tool change before it.
- **Every G30 goes through `retract()`.** `retract()` is the only place the post writes `G30`, and it is called from two places: the tool change in `startPreamble` and `onClose`. The `#110` after-operation home is not a path here: `tormach.cps` does not declare `afterModes`, so the engine refuses a stop or a home by name (crates/post/src/post/js.rs:165-168). A section that opens without a fresh tool change also starts with `aNow` cleared, because `endPreamble` runs at every section end.
- **The order after an index is still safe.** `G53 G0 Z0` comes first, then `G0 A..`, then `G0 X Y` at the top of Z, and only then does Z come down (`xyUnknown` is set after the index, :497-499). The kit program shows that order on all three faces.
- **The pins are tight.** One pin covers a tool change on the same face: `G30` and `M6`, then `G0 A90` after the `M6`, with `G53 G0 Z0` on the line before it. The other covers a same-tool continuation on the same face: one `M6`, and both sections still re-index.
- **The docs match the code.** README steps 3 (swept radius at the safe Z) and 4 (a bare G30 moves A), and checklist items 3 (every operation has its own `G0 A..` after its `T.. M6`) and 7 (A ends at the stored G30 position's A), describe what the post now writes. Checklist item 2 still holds.
- **The earlier non-blocking notes are handled.** The doc comment moved back onto `find_type` (parse.rs:145). `crates/post/tests/mch_head_search.rs` adds a parser pin on a hand-written tree (a leaf ahead of the head, at the top level and nested, plus a tree with no head). It has a provenance line and a gate map. The swept-radius check is filed as #804 (P2, effort:high, Part of #785), and the decision file records it.
- **Goldens are unchanged in this delta.** `tests/golden/nc/tormach/index_4face_microarc4.nc` and the kit `microarc_test_part.nc` are the same as before: every operation there indexes to a new A anyway. No other post changed.

### Local results (PR head merged with current upstream main, which merged cleanly)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build (`camcraft-post`, `camcraft-app`, the named test binaries) | ok |
| app `tormach_fourth_axis` | 12 passed |
| app `microarc_test_part` | 2 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| app `tormach_post` | 10 passed |
| app `tormach_safe_retract` | 4 passed |
| app `machine` | 33 passed |
| app `machine_library` | 11 passed |
| app lib | 107 passed |
| post lib | 7 passed |
| post `mch_head_search` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Revert check.** I removed the two `aNow = null` lines locally and ran the tests again:
- **Both removed:** both new pins fail (`a_tool_change_on_the_same_face_restates_a_after_the_g30` and `a_same_tool_continuation_on_the_same_face_restates_a`).
- **Only the `endPreamble` line removed:** the continuation pin fails.
- **Only the `retract()` line removed:** everything passes. See the first note below.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **The `retract()` reset is belt-and-braces and is not pinned on its own.** Every `G30` the post writes today comes after an `endPreamble`, which already clears `aNow`, so no test can fail with only that line removed. That is fine to keep: it states the reason (a G30 moves A) right where the G30 is written, and it guards a future G30 inside a section. I mention it only so nobody expects a test to cover it.
- **The body ends with `Refs #785`, not `Fixes #785`.** If this PR is meant to close #785 once the tester confirms, the merge will not close it by itself. That is fine if it is intentional (the hardware check is still owed).
- **Upright sections on an A machine now also write `G53 G0 Z0` / `G0 A0` at every section.** This is the intended cost, recorded in the decision file. It is one extra Z lift per section.
- **Still open from the earlier review, your call:** the spindle and coolant stay on while A turns, and the travel check uses the canonical (-180, 180] angle.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
